newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Start on Jewish homes in Arab Jerusalem this week.
newsitem.headline: Start on Jewish homes in Arab Jerusalem this week.

text.p: Israel will begin surveying work for a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem this week, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman said on Monday.
"It will begin in another day or two," spokesman Shai Bazak told Reuters.
The project, approved by Netanyahu's government last week, has sparked Palestinian outrage and international criticism.
On Monday, going into talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Washington, U.S. President Bill Clinton said he wished Israel had not approved the project.

"I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence, I think it builds mistrust," Clinton told reporters at the start of his Oval Office meeting with President Arafat.
Bazak, asked why the work would not begin on Tuesday, as had been reported earlier by state-owned Channel One television, said: "Because of technical reasons".

Israel's Housing Ministry spokesman Moshe Friedman told Reuters shortly after the Israel television report but before Bazak was available to comment that there had been an intention to begin surveying the land on Tuesday "but someone called me and said there's been a change."
The television also said on Monday: "Our reporter says that if there are no petitions (against building) filed, in two weeks the first contractor will go up to build."
The plan will eventually build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem. The site is called Har Homa by Israel.

Israel's moves in Jerusalem spurred violence in September. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gunbattles after Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel near Islamic holy shrines in East Jerusalem.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised internationally, it later annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future state.

The sides are to begin final status peace talks within the coming weeks at which issues including Jerusalem's status, according to a framework interim peace deal, will be negotiated. The sides are to reach a final peace accord by 1999.
Palestinians view Israeli building in Arab East Jerusalem as preempting negotiations.
